q: Can you *make up* a good story about foxes and wolves?
e: to make up a story is to *create* it.

q: My date *stood me up* last night.
e: stand sb up: to intentionally fail to meet someone when you said you would, especially I don't know if I've been stood up or if she's just late - I'll wait another half hour.

q: He will *transfer ownership of* his business to his oldest son next month.
e: *Transfer ownsership* = turn over, pass the legal ownership to, pass the responsibility to someone else

q: He was *reared* in Ponce by his grandparents.
e: *Rear* = raise a child, bring a child up, help a child develop

q: The Commander *reprimanded* Capt. Whitfield during the company formation.
e: *Reprimand* = call down, scold, chew out, say very negative things to

q: The CD player doesn't work. I have to *return it* to the store.
e: *Take back* = return something

q: *I anticipate* going back home.
e: *Look forward to* = to anticipate = to be eager about doing something

q: I want you to *watch* my kids while I go to the store.
e: *Look after* = watch = guard = protect = keep an eye on

q: Wesley *stopped attending* high school when he was only 14.
e: *Drop out of* = stop attending a school or organization

q: That song really *recalls* good memories of when I lived with my grandmother.
e: *Bring back* = to make you remember something from the past. It brings a memory back to your brain.

q: We *exhausted our supply of* sugar. Go buy some more.
e: *Run out of* = to use up your supply of something

q: He will *aid and support* you no matter what happens.
e: *Stand by* = help = support = aid = assist = give you support

q: Some students *answer discourteously* the teachers.
e: *Talk back to* = answer without politeness = sass = say things to rudely

q: I fainted. Then *I regained consciousness* after 10 minutes.
e: *Come to* = to regain consciousness after being unconsciousness. First, you *pass out* or *faint*. When you then "wake up," we say that you "come to.

q: Dogs and cats don't *act like friends* most of the time.
e: *Get along* = be friendly with each other = maintain a good relationship

q: How much did the total bill at the restaurant *add up to*?
e: *Come to* = add up to = total

q: You'd better *adhere to* the speed limit between here and Sacramento.
e: *Stick to* = adhere to = obey = follow

q: That little boy certainly *acts like* his father.
e: *Take after* = to act like = to do what someone else has done = to imitate

q: My father doesn't *have a favorable opinion of* people who smoke cigars.
e: *Approve of* = have a favorable opinion of = think something is OK

q: When you drive, you must *obey and follow* the traffic laws.
e: *Adhere to* = follow = stick to = obey

q: Don't *ridicule* other people's mistakes in class.
e: *Laugh at* = make fun of = ridicule = deride

q: The fire alarm *started ringing* right in the middle of my speech. The bell _____.
e: To "go off" means to sound, explode, ring

q: In the middle of his speech, he *went off the deep end*.
e: to go off the deep end = to act crazily, insanely. To go into a violent rage.

q: *Put* your hat out in the hall on a hook.
e: To put something on a hook = to hang it up

q: My cousin *stopped attending* school when he was only 11 years old.
e: drop out of = to stop attending something or to stop participating in an organized group

q: He stood in line for an hour at the DMV. “Stood in line” means:
e: Stand in line (*US*) = queue (UK).

q: Which kind of dessert did he *choose*?
e: to pick out = choose = select

q: How can you *account for* his low test scores?
e: to account for = explain = give reasons for why something is the way it is

q: I want you to *think over* that job offer before you say no.
e: *Think over* = consider, think about it seriously, don't refuse it yet

q: We can always *rely on* Gerald to help us.
e: count on = rely on = depend on

q: You should *review* this vocabulary list before we take the test.
e: go over = review = look at again = study

q: The police are *investigating* the murder of my neighbor's nephew.
e: to investigate = to look into = to search for evidence

q: Please *discard* all these old magazines.
e: discard = throw away = throw out = toss out = toss away = to get rid of

q: I wish you wouldn't *mention* the subject of AIDS in the classroom.
e: to mention = to bring a subject up = to introduce a topic in the discussion

q: The unit was unable to *accomplish* the mission as ordered.
e: carry out = to accomplish = to do = to completely conclude something

q: Can a normal person *exist on* just $200 per month in Oklahoma City?
e: phrasal verb exist on = live on = subsist on = survive on Can a prisoner *exist on* nothing but bread and water for six months?

q: He *messed up* his speech by forgetting his second point.
e: mess up = ruin = make a mistake = fouled up

q: *I dropped off* during the history lecture.
e: *Drop off* = to fall asleep (while sitting up in a chair)

q: I cannot *accept* any additional duties at this time.
e: *Take on* = accept, agree to perform extra work

q: He *created* an interesting game for his students to play.
e: *Think up* = create, invent, make up

q: We will *handle* tag questions next week.
e: two-word verb to deal with = handle = treat = study or discuss

q: Craig is *well-informed about* everything in Albania.
e: to be up on = to have knowledge about something, to be well-informed about it. I'm not up on all the new rap singers my friends watch on *mtv*.

q: My parents are going to *do over* my grandmother's house in Cleveland.
e: do over = redecorate = improve the appearance of = make something look new again

q: Where did you *pick up* those bad words?
e: *Pick up* = learn something informally, just by hearing or seeing it, without studying.

q: I cannot *take in* all this information at once.
e: *Take in* = understand, absorb in the brain, comprehend

q: My brother is going to *run for* mayor next year.
e: *Run for* = to try to win a political office or position

q: *Carefully consider all the details* before you do it.
e: phrasal verb think through = carefully consider everything in advance

q: We need to *strengthen* the final paragraphs of this report.
e: *Beef up* = to make something stronger. (adding more meat to a weak, watery soup or stew)

q: I want you to *continue* studying.
e: keep on = to continue Keep on answering these questions.

q: We will have to *postpone* the picnic until next week.
e: *Put off* = postpone = delay= do it later, not now. Are they going to put off the next ECL until next month?

q: The ball game was *canceled*.
e: *Call off* = cancel not to be rescheduled

q: Just *wait* a second. I'll get the answer for you.
e: *Hold on* = wait a little bit

q: What time did you *stop sleeping* this morning?
e: *Wake up* = stop sleeping *get up* = leave the bed You usually wake up first. Then, you get up.

q: The owner of the restaurant himself *served* us.
e: *Wait on* = to serve the customer in a restaurant or store. The store was so crowded that we couldn't find a clerk to wait on us.

q: Which shirt did you finally *choose*?
e: *Pick out* = select = choose

q: In Japan, many people *remove* their shoes when they enter a house.
e: *Take off* = remove an item of clothing. Take off your hat when you enter a building.

q: Please *submit your paper* before 2:35.
e: *Turn in* = to hand in = to submit = to give something to someone after completing it

q: You have to *extinguish* that cigarette before you board the airplane.
e: *Put out* = extinguish a fire or a light

q: When will your father's flight *arrive*?
e: *To get in* = arrive = reach the destination

q: I need to *discuss* a serious problem with the supervisor.
e: *Talk over* = discuss, converse with someone We talked over all the old times we had in high school.

q: Don't *discard* your DLI books after graduation. You can use them later.
e: *Throw away* = discard = throw out = put in the garbage = get rid of

q: I'm going to *select* a nice box of chocolates for my mother.
e: *Pick out* = select = choose

q: It took the firemen over five hours to *extinguish* the fire.
e: *Put out* = extinguish = to stop a fire = to stop the light

q: I can't answer these questions! *I quit*!
e: *Give up* = to quit = to stop trying = to surrender

q: You don't have to stand up. *Be seated*.
e: *Sit down* = stop standing

q: *Increase* the volume. I can't hear anything.
e: *Turn up* = increase volume = make it louder

q: The supervisors will not *tolerate* cheating on the tests.
e: *Put up with* = tolerate = let something happen

q: *Review* your notes tonight.
e: Look over = review = study = examine = look at

q: Why don't you *visit us casually* after the game?
e: *Drop in* = to visit casually, not at any specific time

q: You must *complete* application in black ink.
e: *Fill out* = write information in all the blocks = complete all of the form

q: The soldiers ran out of ammo and had to *surrender*.
e: *Give up* = surrender = stop fighting = stop trying to do something you want to do. He didn't know the answer, so he gave up after two minutes.

q: He *removed* a gun from his coat pocket.
e: *Take out* = remove Take your I.D.

q: When will you *finish* your homework?
e: *Get through with* = finish = conclude = end doing something

q: I want you to *remove* my name from your mailing list.
e: *Cross off* = to remove, to eliminate, to omit, to draw a line through so as to cancel

q: It's hot now. I think I'll *store* all my sweaters for the summer.
e: *Put away* = put something in storage, put something in a different place for later use.

q: The Commander *supervises* 138 people in Echo Company.
e: *To be over* = to be in charge of, to be the boss of, to supervise or command

q: You may *enter* the bus now.
e: *Get on* = board a large vehicle like a bus, train, plane or enter a large transportation vehicle

q: When you are driving near a school, *be careful of* children.
e: *Look out for* = be careful, watch out, pay attention, be alert

q: You can always *depend on* Ellen and Craig to give the right answers.
e: *Count on* = depend on = rely on

q: The police officers will *search* your luggage at the airport.
e: *Go through* = to search inside things, looking for something

q: We need to *review* chapters 3 and 4 today.
e: *Go over* = review = look at = review quickly

q: If you want a different pencil, *raise* your hand.
e: *Hold up* = raise something Hold up your books so I can see them.

q: Before you buy that coat, you should *determine it if fits well*.
e: *Try on* = to put clothing on to check the fit

q: He *boarded* the airplane in Portland.
e: *Get on* = to board a vehicle, like a plane, bus, ship, train

q: I need to go to the library to *borrow* a book.
e: *Check out* = to borrow the book from the library. *Return* the book = check in the book.

q: Blake told me to *get lost*.
e: *Go away* = leave me alone = stop bothering me = get lost

q: *Telephone* the dentist and make an appointment for me, OK?
e: *Call up* = make a telephone call

q: Who will *take care of* your dogs while you're on vacation?
e: *Look after* = take care of = watch = keep an eye on = be responsible for

q: I will *leave the hotel* at 10 a.m.
e: *Check out* = leave a place = sign out = pay any final bills and leave. You can check out of the hotel or from the military unit you are assigned to.

q: Blake will *assume control of* the family business next year.
e: *Take over* = assume control of something. Mr. Barrow is retiring next month, and I think Mrs. Whitfield will take over as chief of that department.

q: You need to *remain informed about* events in Cyprus.
e: *Keep up on* = remain informed about = stay current by following the news

q: The meeting should *conclude* around 3:00.
e: *Wind up* = conclude = end = finish

q: We *expected him to come* for an hour before we finally left without him.
e: *Wait for* = not leave until someone arrives = expect someone to arrive

q: Young people *learn at random* a lot of bad slang words in the streets.
e: *Pick up* = to learn things at random, not by studying He's picked up this very bad habit of correcting me every time I try to tell him something.

q: *I ordered through the mail* several new CDs.
e: *Send for* = to order something through the mail

q: We are planning a big party. Would you like to *participate*?
e: *Be in on* = participate = be a part of = share in the activity

q: I will *briefly visit* my friend in the hospital on my way home tonight.
e: *Look in on* = briefly stop to visit someone when you are going somewhere else

q: I was strolling through the Mall when *I accidentally met* an old friend from high school.
e: *Run into* = meet accidentally, meet by chance, encounter someone unexpectedly.

q: My parents bought an old house, so they can *redecorate* it.
e: *Do over* = redecorate an old room or house. The house was cheap, but doing it over cost us a lot.

q: When you get things at the store, *mark those items on the list*.
e: *Check something off* = to mark items on a list to show that you have taken care of them.

q: We should each *contribute* $2 and but the teacher a nice present.
e: *Chip in* = to contribute money to buy something as a group

q: Before you buy a car, you must *test drive it to determine what it's like*.
e: *Try out* = to test something to see if you like it. You would *try out* a car, a gun, a boat.

q: My brother got 30 years in prison because he tried to *rob* a bank.
e: *Hold up* = to rob When you point a gun at someone, he usually *holds* his hands *up* in the air.

q: The teacher always *asks me to talk* when I don't know the answer to the question.
e: *Call on* = to ask someone to talk = to say someone's name in order for that person to speak

q: The number of students from Georgia has *decreased* in the past few months.
e: *Drop off* = to decrease in number = to lessen = to become smaller in number+

q: How do you *explain* your unusually high ECL score?
e: *Account for* = to explain why something is the way it is

q: When you go walking in the woods, *be careful of* snakes and spiders.
e: *Look out for* = be careful about = pay attention

q: The boss *requires* prompt arrival and good work.
e: *Insist on* = demand = require

q: I will not *tolerate* any more cheating on the tests!
e: *Put up with* = tolerate = allow to happen

q: The children *did not go to bed* until after midnight.
e: *Stay up* = not go to bed

q: We must *begin to consider* prepositions next week.
e: *Take up* = begin to consider = start doing something He's going to take up tennis next summer.

q: There was a big nail *protruding* from the wall. I tore my pants on it.
e: *Stick out* = protrude = reach beyond the surface

q: Before you ask for a reassignment, *consider* the matter *carefully*.
e: *Think* something *over* = consider it carefully, think about all the possible advantages and disadvantages

q: If I have to sit in that hot classroom another hour, I'll *fall asleep*.
e: *Drop off* = fall asleep while sitting up. The movie was so boring that I dropped off during the first hour.

q: Before becoming engaged, Craig needs to *formally visit* Beatrice's parents.
e: *Call on* = to visit formally = to announce ahead of time that you want to visit and to arrive on time, perhaps dressed up and bringing gifts

q: I was unemployed for 6 months and *stopped making* my monthly house and car payments.
e: *Get behind in* = stop doing something you are regularly supposed to do because I was sick.

q: When will the boss be able to *inspect* the new equipment?
e: *Check out* = to look at something = to inspect = to see how something is

q: The fire alarm bell *rang* at 9:25.
e: *Go off* = to explode = to activate = to ring Things that can go off are bombs, grenades, alarms signals, bells, alarm clocks, timers

q: He was *forced out of* the military after 13 years of service.
e: *Boot out* = kick out = fire =dismiss = force out

q: Trevor and Curtis are going to *duke it out*.
e: *Fight*. A slang expression for your fists is your *dukes*. "Put up your dukes!" = Prepare to fight.

q: The firemen were able to *extinguish* the fire in less than 30 minutes.
e: put out = extinguish

q: The plane *left* the airport at 0900.
e: two-word verb *leave* = *take off* past tense = *it took off*

q: We *finished* the test 30 minutes early.
e: two-word verb *to get through with* = to finish, complete, end, conclude something

q: He *turned down* a job offer in Oregon.
e: turn down = refuse to accept = decline = reject = say "no" to

q: The student *fell asleep* during the graduation speeches.
e: *Drop off* = fall asleep, often without meaning to.

q: My brother is going to *formally visit* his fiancée’s family next week.
e: to call on = to visit *fiormally*

q: The Commander *reprimanded* Capt. Barrow during formation.
e: reprimand = call down = scold = give a tongue-lashing to= chew out

q: I was *brought up* by my grandparents in a small town.
e: to bring up = to raise = to rear = to bring up = to help grow up

q: He *perked up* when he heard his name mentioned.
e: perk up = become alert = become attentive = pay attention = listen intently

e: *Get used to* is followed by an -ing form: to become accustomed to doing something.

e: *Get used to* + -ing describes the process of becoming accustomed.

q: She has finally _____ driving on the left.
e: *Got used to* + -ing marks the completed process of adapting.

q: The barrier _____ vehicles from entering the compound.
e: *Prevent somebody from doing something* means to stop them doing it.

e: *Prevent from* is the correct pattern. *Avoid* is not followed by *from*.

q: Poor weather _____ the helicopter from taking off.
e: *Prevented from taking off* means stopped it from doing so.

e: act up = (of a machine) not work properly; (of a person) behave badly.

e: act up = cause pain or trouble (a body part, a machine).

e: add on = add an extra part to something that already exists.

q: If you rent a car at the airport, the agent may *add on* insurance and GPS charges at the counter.
e: add on = include something extra, such as an extra charge.

q: We had planned a fishing trip for the long weekend, but Mike ______ at the last minute because his unit was put on alert.

e: bail out = (of a pilot) jump from an aircraft with a parachute.

q: We're *banking on* good weather for Saturday's outdoor graduation ceremony.
e: bank on = rely on; expect something to happen.

q: You shouldn't *rely on* the shuttle bus being on time; it's late almost every morning.

q: The security camera footage *bore out* the guard's account of what happened at the gate.

q: After standing in formation for two hours in the July heat, one recruit *blacked out* and had to be carried to the aid station.
e: black out = suddenly lose consciousness for a short time.

q: The storm knocked down power lines and ______ most of the city for nearly six hours.
e: black out = cause a loss of electric power in an area (also: faint).

e: blow over = pass and be forgotten without serious effects.

q: The forecast says the storm should ______ by midnight, so our flight will probably leave on time in the morning.
e: blow over = (of a storm) pass and end.

q: In the end, choosing between the two apartments *boils down to* how far you want to drive to work every day.
e: boil down to = have as the main point or basic cause.

q: Most of the complaints about the dining facility *are basically a matter of* poor planning.
e: boil down to = be, in its simplest form, about something.

q: The counselor warned that *bottling up* your feelings after a deployment can lead to serious problems later.
e: bottle up = keep strong feelings inside instead of showing them.

q: Jenna ______ her frustration for months until she finally exploded at a staff meeting.
e: bottle up = hide strong feelings for a long time.

q: Sales dropped sharply in the spring, but the company *bounced back* by the end of the year.
e: bounce back = recover quickly after a problem.

q: Sergeant Lopez had knee surgery in May, but he *recovered quickly* and passed his fitness test in August.
e: bounce back = recover quickly after an illness or injury.

q: After ten years of selling only bicycles, the shop *branched out* into outdoor gear and camping equipment.

q: Although she trained as an aircraft mechanic, Maria hopes to ______ into avionics after she reenlists.

q: Before the promotion board, Corporal Diaz spent two weeks *brushing up on* Army regulations and customs.
e: brush up on = improve knowledge or a skill you have partly forgotten.

q: If you're going to work at the embassy in Paris, you'd better *refresh your knowledge of* French.
e: brush up on = practice and improve something you learned before.

q: If you want to pass the language exam in June, you'll have to *buckle down* and study every evening.
e: buckle down = start working hard and seriously.

q: After failing his first inspection, Private Kim ______ and made sure his gear was perfect every morning.

q: Guess who I *bumped into* at the Atlanta airport? My roommate from basic training!

e: bump into = meet by chance (bump off = kill, slang).

q: Street vendors were quick to *cash in on* the huge crowds at the Fourth of July parade.
e: cash in on = make money or gain an advantage from a situation.

q: Several companies tried to ______ the fitness craze by selling expensive protein bars.
e: cash in on = take advantage of a situation to make money.

q: The roof of the old warehouse *caved in* under the weight of the heavy snow.
e: cave in = fall down or inward; collapse.

q: After weeks of pressure from the drivers, management ______ and agreed to replace the old heaters.
e: cave in = finally agree after pressure (held out = continued to resist).

q: The new commander promised to *clamp down on* drunk driving among junior soldiers.
e: clamp down on = take strong action to stop something.

q: City police are ______ illegal parking near the stadium on game days.
e: clamp down on = deal strictly with something to stop it.

q: We have until Friday to *clear out* the old barracks before the renovation crew arrives.
e: clear out = empty a place by removing everything from it.

q: The officer told the crowd to ______ because the building had to be searched.
e: clear out = leave a place quickly.

q: Police helicopters *closed in on* the stolen truck as it left the highway.

q: The search team was *getting closer to* the missing hiker when his phone signal suddenly stopped.
e: close in on = come closer and closer to someone or something.

q: I think I'm *coming down with* a cold; my throat has been sore all day.
e: come down with = become sick with an illness.

q: Two days before the trip, our daughter ______ chickenpox, so we had to cancel everything.
e: come down with = catch an illness.

q: The plan for a new firing range *came up against* strong opposition from local residents.
e: come up against = have to deal with a problem or opposition.

q: Our team *was faced with* several technical problems when we tried to install the new software.
e: come up against = face a difficulty (come up with = think of an idea).

q: Both drivers were shouting, so the officer told them to *cool down* before they explained what happened.
e: cool down = become calmer.

q: After a long run, walk and stretch for ten minutes to let your body ______ slowly.
e: cool down = become less hot; warm up = prepare before exercise.

q: Military police *cordoned off* the parking lot while the bomb squad examined the abandoned bag.
e: cordon off = put a barrier around an area to keep people out.

q: Firefighters ______ the area around the chemical plant and told residents to stay indoors.
e: cordon off = surround an area with tape, ropes, or guards so no one can enter.

q: The airline has *cracked down on* passengers who bring oversized bags into the cabin.
e: crack down on = start dealing much more strictly with something.

q: The state is *taking strict measures against* drivers who text behind the wheel.
e: crack down on = act strongly to stop a bad or illegal activity.

q: The doctor told him to *cut back on* coffee and get more sleep.
e: cut back on = reduce the amount of something.

q: Because of budget problems, the unit had to ______ overtime and travel for the rest of the year.
e: cut back on = reduce spending or use.

q: The phone company *cut off* our service because we forgot to pay the bill.
e: cut off = stop a supply or service.

q: We were in the middle of a video call with my brother in Germany when we got ______.
e: get cut off = be disconnected during a call.

q: Heavy snow *isolated* the mountain village for nearly a week.
e: cut off = separate a place from other places so no one can reach it.

q: Halfway to the airport, it *dawned on* Rick that his passport was in his checked bag.
e: dawn on = (an idea or fact) become clear to someone for the first time.

q: It didn't ______ me until later that the stranger at the gate had been testing our security.
e: It dawned on me that ... = I suddenly realized that ...

q: The applause finally *died down*, and the general began his speech.
e: die down = gradually become weaker or quieter.

q: Once the excitement about the new gym *had decreased*, only a few people used it regularly.
e: die down = become less strong (take off = become popular).

q: When the food arrived, the hungry soldiers *dug in* without waiting for the speeches to end.

q: The infantry company was ordered to ______ on the ridge and hold it until reinforcements arrived.
e: dig in = prepare a defensive position and stay there.

q: The cooks *dished out* hot chili to everyone coming off the night shift.
e: dish out = serve food to people.

q: Sergeant Brooks can ______ criticism all day, but he gets upset when someone criticizes him.
e: dish out = give out criticism or advice freely to others.

q: The base library *did away with* late fees last year.
e: do away with = get rid of; abolish.

q: Many banks have ______ paper statements and now send everything by email.
e: do away with = stop using something; make away with = steal.

q: During the blackout, volunteers *doled out* bottled water and blankets at the community center.
e: dole out = give out something to several people.

q: The charity *distributed* food and clothing to families after the hurricane.
e: dole out = distribute, give out in portions.

q: The contract negotiations *dragged on* for months, and both sides grew tired of waiting.
e: drag on = continue for too long.

q: The safety lecture ______ for three hours, and half the class was falling asleep.
e: drag on = last much longer than people want.

q: The staff officers *drew up* a detailed evacuation plan for the embassy.
e: draw up = prepare and write a plan or document.

q: Before the move, we *made* a list of everything that needed to be packed.
e: draw up a list = write a list (draw on = use your experience or resources).

q: The movie was so slow that I *drifted off* before the end.
e: drift off = gradually fall asleep.

q: He was so tired after guard duty that he ______ in his chair while his wife was still talking.
e: drift off = fall asleep slowly (drift apart = become less close).

q: The noise of the generators *drowned out* the radio messages from headquarters.
e: drown out = be so loud that another sound cannot be heard.

q: The fans cheered so loudly that they ______ the announcer completely.
e: drown out = cover a sound with a louder one.

q: Funding for the youth sports program *dried up* when the main sponsor left town.
e: dry up = (of money, work, supplies) stop being available.

q: There was no rain for months, and the river near the village ______ completely.
e: dry up = (of a river or lake) lose all its water.

q: The pain in my shoulder *eased off* after a few days of rest.
e: ease off = become less strong or less intense.

q: Traffic usually *becomes lighter* after nine o'clock, so we'll leave then.
e: ease off = decrease (pick up = increase).

q: Rising fuel prices are *eating into* the trucking company's profits.
e: eat into = use up or reduce part of something, such as money or time.

q: All this extra paperwork ______ the time we should be spending on real training.
e: eat into = take away part of your time or money.

q: In the final race, the young lieutenant *edged out* a much more experienced runner.
e: edge out = beat someone by a very small amount.

q: The Navy team *barely defeated* the Air Force team in the last seconds of the game.
e: edge out = win against someone by a small margin.

q: The crowd *egged on* the two boxers, shouting for a knockout.
e: egg on = encourage someone, usually to do something risky or foolish.

q: Jason wouldn't have climbed the water tower if his buddies hadn't ______.
e: egg someone on = push someone to do something foolish.

q: Our workload is heavy in the spring, but it usually *evens out* over the year.
e: even out = become equal, level, or steady.

q: Use a rake to ______ the gravel before you lay the paving stones.
e: even out = make a surface flat and level.

q: Sooner or later, you'll have to *face up to* the fact that the car needs a new engine.
e: face up to = accept and deal with a difficult fact.

q: Instead of blaming his crew, the captain *accepted and dealt with* his own mistakes.
e: face up to = admit a problem and deal with it.

q: My grandmother almost *fell for* a phone scam from someone claiming to be from her bank.
e: fall for = be tricked into believing something.

q: He ______ a nurse he met at the base hospital, and they got married a year later.
e: fall for someone = start to love someone.

q: Only two recruits *were deceived by* the instructor's trick question.
e: fall for = be fooled by a trick.

q: The spokesperson *fended off* reporters' questions about the accident.
e: fend off = defend yourself against questions, attacks, or competition.

q: The small hardware store has managed to ______ competition from the big chains for over twenty years.
e: fend off = resist or keep away (fend for yourself = take care of yourself).

q: Interest in the book club *fizzled out* after a few months.
e: fizzle out = gradually end in a weak or disappointing way.

q: The storm *gradually lost its strength* before it reached the coast.
e: fizzle out = slowly become weaker and end.

q: Fighting *flared up* again along the border after a week of calm.
e: flare up = suddenly start again or become more intense.

q: My allergies always ______ in the spring when the trees are blooming.
e: flare up = (an illness or pain) suddenly get worse.

q: The landlord promised to fix the heating, but he never *followed through*.
e: follow through = do what you promised or planned until it is complete.

q: If you warn your kids about a punishment, you have to ______; otherwise they won't take you seriously.
e: follow through = carry out what you said you would do.

q: I had to *fork out* $300 for a new phone after mine fell into the lake.
e: fork out = pay money, usually unwillingly.

q: Parents often have to *pay a lot of money* for school trips and sports equipment.
e: fork out = spend a lot of money on something.

q: In many offices, wearing jeans on a Monday is still *frowned on*.
e: frown on = disapprove of something.

q: Most units ______ soldiers who show up late to formation, even by a minute.
e: frown on = think that something or someone's behavior is wrong.

q: Stores are *gearing up* for the holiday shopping season by hiring extra staff.
e: gear up (for) = get ready for an activity or event.

q: The battalion is *preparing* for a major training exercise in the desert next month.
e: gear up = prepare for something big.

q: The briefing *glossed over* the risks and focused only on the benefits.
e: gloss over = treat a problem as unimportant and avoid details.

q: A good after-action review doesn't ______ mistakes; it looks at them honestly.
e: gloss over = hide or ignore problems instead of dealing with them.

q: The air show will *go ahead* as planned unless the wind gets stronger.
e: go ahead = happen as planned.

q: "Can I borrow your truck this weekend?" "______. The keys are on the hook by the door."
e: Go ahead = Yes, you may; do it.

q: The commander gave permission for the exercise to *proceed* once the weather cleared.
e: go ahead = begin or continue (go under = fail, sink).

q: Staff Sergeant Moore is *gunning for* a spot on the Special Forces selection course.
e: gun for = try very hard to get something.

q: Our team won the championship last year, so this season every other team is ______ us.
e: gun for = try hard to defeat or attack someone.

q: The thief *handed over* the stolen wallet as soon as the officers arrived.
e: hand over = give something to someone, often because you are told to.

q: At the end of my shift, I ______ the keys and the logbook to the next guard.
e: hand over = pass something or responsibility to another person.

q: *Hang on* a second; I need to check whether the colonel is free.
e: hang on = wait a short time.

q: The road is very bumpy, so ______ tight to the handle above the door.
e: hang on = hold something tightly.

q: I'm sorry, could you *wait for a moment*? I have another call coming in.
e: hang on = wait briefly, especially on the phone (hang up = end a call).

q: The police *held back* the crowd while the ambulance drove through.
e: hold back = stop people from moving forward.

q: I think she's ______ something; she won't tell us everything she knows about the accident.
e: hold back = not tell all the information you have.

q: We decided to *hold off* on buying a new car until after the move.
e: hold off (on) = delay doing something.

q: Luckily, the rain ______ until the graduation ceremony was over.
e: hold off = (of rain or bad weather) not start.

q: Our water supply won't *hold out* for more than three days if the pipes aren't repaired.
e: hold out = last; continue to be enough.

q: The surrounded troops *continued to resist* until the relief force arrived.
e: hold out = keep resisting an enemy or pressure (give in = surrender).

q: The hotel managers tried to *hush up* the food poisoning case, but a guest posted about it online.
e: hush up = keep something bad secret.

q: The coach was fired for trying to ______ a player's failed drug test.
e: hush up = hide something so the public does not find out.

q: The two departments met on Monday to *iron out* their differences over the new schedule.
e: iron out = solve small problems or differences.

q: There are still a few bugs in the new app, but the developers expect to have them ______ by next week.
e: iron out = fix problems so that something works smoothly.

q: The duty clerk *jotted down* the caller's name and number on a sticky note.
e: jot down = write something quickly.

q: During the briefing, I *quickly wrote* the grid coordinates on the back of my hand.
e: jot down = make a quick written note.

q: Make sure the backup generator *kicks in* automatically when the power goes out.
e: kick in = start to work or have an effect.

q: The new pay rate doesn't ______ until January, so your December check will stay the same.
e: kick in = begin to take effect.

q: The county fair *kicks off* on Friday evening with a fireworks display.
e: kick off = begin (an event).

q: The commander *started* the ceremony with a moment of silence.
e: kick off = start an event or activity (put off = delay).

q: The game ______ at 7 p.m., so let's get to the stadium early.
e: kick off = (of a game or event) start.

q: We usually *knock off* early on Fridays during the summer.
e: knock off (informal) = stop working for the day.

q: If you pay in cash, the dealer says he'll ______ ten percent.
e: knock off = take an amount away from a price.

q: Tired and stressed, the trainee *lashed out* at his roommate over a missing towel.
e: lash out (at) = suddenly attack someone with words or violence.

q: After the loss, the coach *strongly criticized* the referees in front of reporters.
e: lash out at = criticize someone angrily.

q: The plant *laid off* nearly half its workers when orders from the Army dropped.
e: lay off = end workers' jobs because there is not enough work.

q: Many workers were ______ when the mall closed, and some are still looking for jobs.
e: be laid off = lose your job because there is not enough work (laid up = sick in bed).

q: The trucking company plans to *end the jobs of* forty drivers this winter.
e: lay off = dismiss workers, often for economic reasons.

q: When I told my parents about the crash, I *left out* the part about the broken windshield.
e: leave out = not include; omit.

q: Please don't ______ anyone when you send the invitations for the retirement party.
e: leave out = not include someone or something.

q: His name was *omitted* from the list of graduates by mistake.
e: leave out = omit (left over = remaining).

q: The rain didn't *let up* until late afternoon, so the range stayed closed.
e: let up = become weaker or stop.

q: Our drill sergeant never ______; he pushed us hard from the first day to the last.
e: let up = make less effort; become less intense.

q: After rising for six months, home prices near the base have *leveled off*.
e: level off = stop rising or falling and stay steady.

q: The aircraft climbed to 30,000 feet and then *began to fly horizontally*.
e: level off = (of an aircraft) stop climbing and fly level.

q: After the robbery, the suspects *lay low* in a mountain cabin for two weeks.
e: lie low (past: lay low) = stay hidden and avoid attention.

q: After his embarrassing mistake at the staff meeting, Tom decided to ______ for a while and avoid attention.
e: lie low = keep out of sight for a while.

q: The new rifle scope *lived up to* its reputation for accuracy.
e: live up to = be as good as expected.

q: As the son of a decorated general, he always felt pressure to ______ the family name.
e: live up to = meet the high standards others expect.

q: The school was *locked down* for two hours after someone reported a man with a weapon nearby.
e: lock down = close a place so no one can enter or leave, for security.

q: After an intruder was spotted near the flight line, security forces ______ the entire base.
e: lock down = secure a place and restrict movement in and out.

q: After the system upgrade, nobody in the personnel office could ______ to the database until IT reset their passwords.
e: log on (to) = enter a computer system with your password; log off = leave it.

q: Remember to *log on* with your new password before the online safety course closes at 1600.
e: log on = connect to a computer system or website, usually with a username and password.

q: Our rations were delayed by the storm, so the platoon had to *make do with* crackers and canned fruit for two days.
e: make do with = manage with what is available, even if it is not ideal.

q: Until the new furniture arrives, the family will have to *manage with* two folding chairs and an air mattress.
e: make do with = manage with something less than ideal; do away with = get rid of; come up with = think of.

q: Before the deployment, the logistics officer ______ every stage of the move, from loading the trucks to arriving at the port.
e: map out = plan in detail. hand out = distribute; wipe out = destroy; pass out = faint.

q: Over the weekend, Sergeant Ruiz *mapped out* a six-week fitness program for soldiers who had failed the run.
e: map out = plan something carefully, step by step.

q: The base exchange *marked down* last year's laptops to make room for the new models.
e: mark down = lower the price of goods (opposite: mark up).

q: Every item in the clearance aisle has been *reduced in price* by 50 percent.
e: mark down = reduce the price. mark out = draw lines to show an area; put off = postpone; turn down = refuse.

q: Specialist Grant was on guard duty during the unit party, so he ______ the barbecue and the awards.
e: miss out on = not get to enjoy something good because you are absent or too late.

q: Many travelers *miss out on* cheaper fares because they book their flights at the last minute.
e: miss out on = lose the chance to get or enjoy something.

q: I always *mix up* the Garcia twins because they have the same haircut and wear the same uniform.
e: mix up = confuse one person or thing with another.

q: Please label the boxes clearly so the movers don't ______ our household goods with our neighbors' things.
e: mix up A with B = confuse A and B, take one for the other.

q: With her excellent evaluations, Sergeant Kim expects to *move up* quickly in the logistics field.
e: move up = rise to a higher position or rank.

q: The general's visit was *changed to an earlier date*, so we had only two days to prepare.
e: move up = make an event happen earlier. put off = postpone; hold up = delay.

q: After a fourteen-hour shift, the radio operator kept *nodding off* at the console.
e: nod off = fall asleep for a short time, often without wanting to.

q: The lecture on supply regulations was so dull that half the class had ______ before the break.
e: nod off = fall asleep, especially when bored or tired.

q: The gate guard *wrote down* the license plate of every car that came onto the post after midnight.
e: note down = write down. turn down = refuse; knock down = hit to the ground or destroy.

q: The interpreter *noted down* every number the caller gave so she could repeat it accurately.
e: note down = make a written note of something.

q: Soldiers who don't want their photos posted on the unit's website may *opt out* by signing this form.
e: opt out (of) = decide not to be included in something.

q: You are automatically enrolled in the savings plan unless you ______ in writing before March 1.
e: opt out = choose not to participate. You opt in to join something you are not automatically part of.

q: Eventually, Private Lewis *confessed to* losing the night-vision goggles during the exercise.
e: own up to = admit a mistake. make up for = compensate; look up to = admire; stand up to = resist.

q: The cadet *owned up* to cheating before the investigation had even started.
e: own up (to) = admit that you did something wrong.

q: If the new job in Denver doesn't *pan out*, we'll move back to Texas to be near my parents.
e: pan out = turn out well; it is often used in the negative: didn't pan out.

q: We're not sure yet how the new shift schedule will ______, but the first week looked promising.
e: pan out = develop or turn out. pass out = faint; put out = extinguish; pull out = withdraw.

q: Despite her strong record, Captain Ortiz was *passed over* for the command position in favor of a less experienced officer.
e: be passed over (for) = not be chosen when you expected to be.

q: Some employees feel they have been *ignored for promotion* simply because they work nights.
e: be passed over for promotion = not be chosen for it. pass out = faint; turn over = give control to someone.

q: Sergeant Diaz *passed up* a promotion so she could stay near her sick mother in Ohio.
e: pass up = refuse or not use an opportunity.

q: This deal on airline tickets is too good to ______; book it before the sale ends tonight.
e: too good to pass up = too good to refuse or miss.

q: The medic *patched up* the soldier's cut hand and sent him back to the range.
e: patch up = treat an injury or repair something quickly, often temporarily.

q: After weeks of silence, the two roommates finally *repaired* their friendship over a pizza.
e: patch up a friendship = make it good again after a quarrel. break up = end a relationship.

q: All those Saturday study sessions *paid off* when Corporal Hayes scored 90 on the ECL.
e: pay off (no object) = bring good results.

q: It took us six years, but we finally ______ the mortgage on our house in El Paso.
e: pay off a debt = pay all of it. lay off = dismiss workers; put off = postpone.

q: The risky decision *proved successful*: the small company's app now has over a million users.
e: pay off = succeed. fall through = fail to happen; break down = stop working.

q: Interest in the new Spanish club *petered out* after a few weeks, and now only three members come.
e: peter out = slowly decrease and then stop.

q: The paved road ______ into a dirt track, so we finished the land navigation course on foot.
e: peter out = gradually become smaller and disappear.

q: The airline plans to *gradually stop using* paper tickets by the end of next year.
e: phase out = stop using step by step. The opposite, phase in, means to introduce gradually.

q: The dining facility is *phasing out* plastic water bottles to reduce waste.
e: phase out = remove or stop using gradually.

q: Good interviewers *pick up on* small changes in a person's voice or body language.
e: pick up on = notice something small or hidden.

q: My daughter is only six, but she ______ the fact that we were worried about my deployment.
e: pick up on = notice something that is not said directly.

q: If you don't answer your messages every day, they will ______ and you'll never catch up.
e: pile up = build up into a large amount.

q: Unpaid bills began to *pile up* after he lost his part-time job.
e: pile up = build up in quantity.

q: Technicians spent all morning trying to *pin down* the cause of the radar failure.
e: pin down = find out or identify something exactly.

q: Nobody at the port could *say exactly* when the shipment would arrive.
e: pin down = establish exactly. hold down = keep low, or keep a job.

q: The company tried to *play down* the data breach, calling it a minor technical issue.
e: play down = make something seem less important (opposite: play up).

q: Although his knee was badly swollen, the runner ______ the injury so he could stay on the team.
e: play down = minimize. play up = exaggerate; show off = try to impress.

q: My laptop died in the middle of the presentation because I had forgotten to ______ the charger.
e: plug in = connect to an electrical outlet. plug up = block a hole.

q: *Plug in* the space heater only after you've checked the cord for damage.
e: plug in = put the plug into an outlet so the machine gets electricity.

q: The investigators *pored over* the flight records for weeks, looking for the smallest error.
e: pore over = examine or read very carefully (do not confuse with pour).

q: For hours the analysts *carefully examined* the satellite photos of the area.
e: pore over = study closely. pour out = flow out; pass over = ignore.

q: The accident victim lost a lot of blood, but the surgeons say she will *pull through*.
e: pull through = survive or recover from a serious illness or injury.

q: Our small restaurant almost closed during the recession, but with help from loyal customers we ______.
e: pull through = get through a difficult time successfully.

q: Bad weather has *pushed back* the parachute jump to Thursday afternoon.
e: push back = postpone, move to a later time.

q: The meeting with the contractors has been *postponed* until after the holiday.
e: push back = postpone. push up (a date) = move it earlier; bring up = mention.

q: During two tours overseas, Sergeant Brooks ______ more than 500 hours of flight time.
e: rack up = accumulate a large number of something.

q: Students who *rack up* credit card debt in college often struggle for years afterward.
e: rack up = build up, often a large amount of something.

q: Our tour guide could *rattle off* the names of every general buried in the cemetery.
e: rattle off = recite quickly and easily from memory.

q: When the colonel asked for the specs, the engineer *quickly listed from memory* the range, weight, and speed of the drone.
e: rattle off = say a list quickly. rattle on = talk for too long.

q: The new mall hopes to *reel in* shoppers with free parking and late hours.
e: reel in = attract (like pulling in a fish).

q: After a twenty-minute fight, my father finally ______ a huge catfish at Lake Texoma.
e: reel in = pull a fish toward you by winding the line. reel off = say a list quickly.

q: The finance office was ordered to *rein in* spending on travel and conferences.
e: rein in = control or restrict (like pulling a horse's reins).

q: The coach had to *control* his star player's temper before it cost the team the championship.
e: rein in = bring under control. turn in = submit; give in = surrender.

q: The first sergeant *roped in* three privates to help set up chairs for the ceremony.
e: rope in = get someone to help, often when they don't really want to.

q: We needed one more player for the volleyball game, so we ______ the chaplain's assistant.
e: rope in = persuade someone to join. rope off = close an area with ropes.

q: Investigators have *ruled out* mechanical failure as the cause of the helicopter crash.
e: rule out = decide that something is not possible or true.

q: The forecast doesn't ______ the possibility of snow on the mountain pass tonight.
e: rule out a possibility = say it cannot happen.

q: Because of my knee injury, the doctor has *excluded* any chance of my returning to airborne school this year.
e: rule out = exclude. carry out = perform; draw up = prepare a document.

q: Thanks to months of practice, Ahmed *sailed through* the oral interview.
e: sail through = pass or complete easily.

q: With her strong math background, Jana ______ the navigation course while others struggled.
e: sail through = do something successfully and easily.

q: Because of the fuel shortage, the battalion had to *reduce the size of* its field exercise.
e: scale back = reduce. scale up = increase; set back = delay.

q: The airline has *scaled back* its winter schedule, dropping flights to three cities.
e: scale back = make smaller or less.

q: When I was a student, I *scraped by* on part-time work and instant noodles.
e: scrape by = survive with just enough money.

q: Many young families on base ______ on one paycheck until the spouse can find work.
e: scrape by = manage with very little money.

q: The detective *saw through* the suspect's story at once; the times didn't match.
e: see through = not be fooled by a lie or trick.

q: The supervisor *was not fooled by* his excuse about a flat tire; it was his third one this month.
e: see through = recognize a lie. see off = say goodbye at a departure; see to = take care of.

q: Firefighters *sealed off* the street while they dealt with the gas leak.
e: seal off = block all the ways into or out of a place.

q: After a suspicious package was found, MPs ______ the parking lot and called the bomb squad.
e: seal off = close an area. set off = cause to explode.

q: Try to *set aside* at least an hour every day for English practice.
e: set aside = keep time or money for a particular purpose.

q: Let's ______ our differences for now and focus on finishing the mission.
e: set aside = put to one side and not let it influence you for now.

q: Every month, Corporal Ellis *saves* part of his paycheck for a new truck.
e: set aside = save money for later. set back = delay; lay off = dismiss workers.

q: After retiring from the Army, my uncle *settled down* in a small town in Vermont.
e: settle down = start living a quiet, stable life in one place.

q: The kids were so excited about the trip that it took them an hour to ______ and go to sleep.
e: settle down = become calm. settle up = pay what you owe.

q: It took me almost two weeks to *shake off* the flu I caught in basic training.
e: shake off = recover from or get rid of something.

q: The driver took several side streets to *escape from* the car that was following him.
e: shake off = escape from someone following you. shake up = upset or reorganize.

q: The battalion will *ship out* to Germany at the end of the month.
e: ship out = leave, especially to go overseas on military duty.

q: The night before he ______ for basic training, Mark had dinner with his whole family.
e: ship out = leave for military service.

q: Volunteers used sandbags to *strengthen* the riverbank before the flood.
e: shore up = support or strengthen. show up = arrive; shut up = stop talking.

q: The company is hiring more engineers to *shore up* its cybersecurity defenses.
e: shore up = make stronger.

q: Jake loves to *show off* his new pickup truck to everyone at the motor pool.
e: show off (something) = proudly show it to impress people.

q: He was ______ in front of his friends when he tried the jump and broke his ankle.
e: show off = behave in a way meant to impress others.

q: The sergeant *shrugged off* his blisters and finished the 12-mile march.
e: shrug off = ignore or treat as minor.

q: Don't just *dismiss* the warning lights on your dashboard; get the car checked.
e: shrug off = dismiss as not important. brush up = improve a skill.

q: The drill sergeant ______ two recruits from the formation and praised their uniforms.
e: single out = choose one or a few from a group for special praise or criticism.

q: Of all the units, the inspector *singled out* the night crew for praise in her report.
e: single out = select one person or group for special mention.

q: The new platoon leader took a few days to *size up* her soldiers before making any changes.
e: size up = observe and form an opinion of.

q: A good pilot can ______ a dangerous situation in seconds and decide what to do.
e: size up = quickly judge or assess a situation.

q: The recruiter told me to *sleep on* the offer and call him back on Monday.
e: sleep on something = delay a decision until the next day.

q: I don't want to rush into buying the house, so let me ______ it and give you an answer tomorrow.
e: sleep on it = think about it overnight. sleep in = stay in bed late; sleep off = recover by sleeping.

q: The cashier *slipped up* and charged me twice for the same item.
e: slip up = make a small, careless error.

q: If anyone *makes an error* during the inspection, the whole squad does extra push-ups.
e: slip up = make a mistake. slip out = leave quietly; step up = increase or take responsibility.

q: The new regulation *spells out* which phones are allowed in secure areas.
e: spell out = explain in a clear, detailed way.

q: Let me ______ the rules one more time: no phones, no food, and no talking during the test.
e: spell out = state something very clearly.

q: Stress at work sometimes *spills over* into family life.
e: spill over = spread from one area into another.

q: The flooding *spread* into the neighboring county, closing several roads.
e: spill over = spread beyond limits. spell out = explain clearly.

q: Make sure your wall locker is *squared away* before the first sergeant comes through.
e: squared away (American, military) = neat, organized and ready.

q: I'll be with you in a minute; I just need to ______ this paperwork for the new arrivals.
e: square away = finish and organize. square off = get ready to fight.

q: Once the storm had passed, the rescue teams were told to *stand down*.
e: stand down = end a state of readiness.

q: After the false alarm, the quick reaction force was ordered to *return to normal status*.
e: stand down = end readiness. stand by = be ready to act; step in = intervene.

q: While the instructor was sick, Sergeant Cole ______ him and taught the morning class.
e: stand in for = replace someone temporarily. stand up for = defend; stand up to = resist.

q: Can you *stand in for* me at the meeting on Tuesday? I have a dental appointment.
e: stand in for = do someone's job for a short time.

q: The company cut salaries by ten percent to *stave off* bankruptcy.
e: stave off = keep something unpleasant away.

q: Drink plenty of water and rest in the shade to ______ heat exhaustion during the march.
e: stave off = prevent. set off = cause something to start.

q: The CEO announced she would *step down* at the end of the year for health reasons.
e: step down = resign from a position.

q: After thirty years at the hospital, Dr. Patel ______ as chief of surgery to spend more time with his grandchildren.
e: step down = leave a job. step up = increase or take responsibility; step in = intervene.

q: Police have *stepped up* patrols near schools since the start of the year.
e: step up = increase the amount or speed of something.

q: When the team leader got hurt, Specialist Vega *took responsibility* and led the squad back to base.
e: step up = act when needed and take responsibility. step aside = move out of the way.

q: If you *stick to* your study schedule, you'll be ready for the ECL in six weeks.
e: stick to = continue to follow a plan or rule.

q: The lawyer told him to ______ the facts and not guess about what happened that night.
e: stick to the facts = say only what is true and known.

q: Before the hurricane hit, families on base ______ bottled water, batteries, and canned food.
e: stock up on = buy a supply of something for later.

q: We always *stock up on* coffee when the commissary has its case-lot sale.
e: stock up on = buy plenty of something.

q: Hikers *stumbled upon* an old army bunker hidden deep in the forest.
e: stumble upon = discover by accident.

q: While browsing online, I *happened to find* a cheap flight to Seoul.
e: stumble upon = find by chance. call upon = ask formally; look upon = regard.

q: The colonel *swore in* twenty new recruits in front of their proud families.
e: swear in = officially admit someone by having them take an oath.

q: The new mayor will be ______ on January 2 at City Hall.
e: be sworn in = take the oath of office. be sworn at = be cursed at.

q: I hate it when the IT guy *talks down to* me just because I don't know the technical terms.
e: talk down to = speak in a superior way to someone.

q: Experienced NCOs know that *speaking condescendingly to* new soldiers only destroys trust.
e: talk down to = treat as inferior. talk back to = answer rudely.

q: Please ______ the break room before you leave; the general is visiting tomorrow.
e: tidy up = put things in order.

q: The hotel staff came in to *tidy up* while we were out at the museum.
e: tidy up = clean and arrange things neatly.

q: An anonymous caller *tipped off* investigators about the stolen equipment.
e: tip off = give secret information to.

q: The smugglers had already left; someone must have ______ the gang about the raid.
e: tip off = warn secretly. tip over = knock over; tell off = scold.

q: The C-17 *touched down* at Ramstein at 0400 local time.
e: touch down = land (an aircraft).

q: The helicopter ______ on the hospital roof, and the medics rushed out with a stretcher.
e: touch down = land. touch up = improve with small changes.

q: The supply clerk finally *tracked down* the missing generator in a warehouse in Kuwait.
e: track down = find after looking hard.

q: Genealogy websites can help you ______ relatives you never knew you had.
e: track down = find by searching.

q: Marshals spent three years trying to *locate* the escaped prisoner.
e: track down = locate. back down = stop insisting; settle down = become calm.

q: If you *trade in* your old phone, the store will give you $200 off a new one.
e: trade in = give an old item to lower the price of a new one.

q: We ______ our minivan for a smaller car when the kids left for college.
e: trade in X for Y = give X as part payment for Y.

q: Thousands of families *tuned in* to watch the live stream of the graduation ceremony.
e: tune in = watch or listen to a broadcast.

q: Don't forget to *watch* Channel 5 tonight at eight; my brother is on the quiz show.
e: tune in to = watch or listen to a channel. tune up = adjust an engine; tone down = make less strong.

q: Once the excitement of the new job *wore off*, I started to miss my old friends.
e: wear off = gradually go away.

q: Don't drive until the effects of the medicine have completely ______.
e: wear off = stop having an effect.

q: The interview process is meant to *weed out* applicants who are not serious about the job.
e: weed out = remove the unwanted ones.

q: An editor's job is to *find and remove* errors before the manual is printed.
e: weed out = find and remove. wear out = use until useless; wind up = end up.

q: During the long flight to Okinawa, we ______ the hours watching movies and doing crossword puzzles.
e: while away the time = pass it pleasantly.

q: Stuck at the airport, the soldiers *whiled away* the afternoon reading and playing chess.
e: while away = spend time lazily or pleasantly.

q: After a long week of field training, the soldiers *wound down* with a cookout at the lake.
e: wind down = relax after stress or work.

q: The factory will *gradually reduce* production over the next year before it closes for good.
e: wind down = reduce gradually before ending. break down = stop working.

q: A single hailstorm *wiped out* the entire wheat harvest in the valley.
e: wipe out = destroy completely.

q: The medical bills almost ______ our savings after my wife's surgery.
e: wipe out = use up or destroy completely.

q: After the holidays, I needed a month at the gym to *work off* the extra pounds.
e: work off = get rid of by physical activity.

q: The young airman ______ his frustration by going for a long run.
e: work off = get rid of a feeling through activity. work up = develop.

q: We should *wrap up* the exercise by Friday and be home for the weekend.
e: wrap up = complete.

q: The general ______ his speech by thanking the families for their support.
e: wrap up = conclude.

q: The detectives are close to *completing* their investigation.
e: wrap up = finish. take up = start; back up = support.

q: Experts had *written off* the young boxer, but he won the title in the fourth round.
e: write off = decide that someone has no chance of success.

q: The bank agreed to *cancel* the small debt because collecting it would cost too much.
e: write off a debt = cancel it. write up = write a report.

q: The analysts quickly *zeroed in on* the problem: a faulty sensor in the left engine.
e: zero in on = direct all attention to.

q: Using GPS data, the rescue helicopter ______ the stranded hikers within an hour.
e: zero in on = aim at or find exactly.

q: Halfway through the PowerPoint briefing, I completely *zoned out* and missed the new schedule.
e: zone out = stop concentrating.

q: Drivers on long, straight highways sometimes *stop paying attention* without realizing it.
e: zone out = lose concentration. pass out = faint.
